Write or revise the agent-facing text below. Every line of it is read by an agent on every
matching turn, so each line must change what the agent does.

- FIRST, CAN A CHECK DO IT? Nothing in CLAUDE.md is a gate. If the rule is mechanical, the
  fix is a test, census or CI step that refuses the mistake by name; propose that instead
  of prose, and write prose only for a judgement no check can make.
- STATE THE BEHAVIOUR. Say what to do, in the imperative, one rule per bullet. A rule that
  only names what to avoid leaves the agent guessing the alternative.
- THE HEADLINE IS THE WHOLE RULE. In CLAUDE.md a bolded headline must be obeyable without
  opening anything; its `→ doctrine/<section>/<rule>.md` pointer holds the evidence (the
  measurement, the PR, the session). A pointer that does not resolve is a bug. A new rule is
  three edits: the headline with its pointer, the body file, and `npm run agents-md`.
- COMPRESS. Cut words that change no behaviour, repeat another rule, or restate the heading.
  Never shorten the 56 frozen pre-migration headlines or bodies
  (test/fixtures/doctrine-pre-migration-W1-T3323.json); shorten the preamble or a newer
  headline instead.
- CITE SYMBOLS, NOT LINE NUMBERS. Line numbers go stale; a symbol name can be searched.
  Name the PR or task that earned the rule.
- A macro row or worker procedure follows the same rules. A worker procedure (`applies-to:`)
  also spends the shared knowledge budget on every matching prompt, so it must be short.

Show the text as a diff against what exists, and say for each changed line which rule above
it serves.

Rules this invokes (CLAUDE.md):

- Plan and task hygiene
